2. Facts, in short, are that a closed fishery by name Duttapara Beel, popularly known as Gacher Jouar fishery, hereinafter, in short, the fishery, situates in the police station Salla, Sunamgonj that as per policy regarding leasing of fishery that has been formulated at the level of Ministry of Land and that circulated for the guidance of the officials at the District level dealing with the matter of leasing fishery, the fishery in question required to be leased out by inviting bid through open tender; that the fishery in question used to be leased out for 3 years, that the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj on 15-3-1998 invited bid through Tender published in the newspapers to lease out the fishery in question, that bid in the previous term i.e. 1402-1404, was at Taka 5,20,000.00, that there was no satisfactory bid for the term 1405-1407 from the Fishermen's Co-operative Society, or from any individual i.e. 25% higher than the previous years in successive five schedules and that at the 6th schedule only the petitioner and another dropped tender and that petitioner's bid was at Taka 3,40,500.00 for the term 1405-1407 BS; that tender Committee in the background of the facts and circumstances as stated hereinbefore and that in the light of the instruction as in Ministry's Memo Dated 28-9-1994 (at Annexure-D to the petition) having found petitioner's bid higher than the other bid made in the schedule accepted petitioner's bid; that thereupon petitioner deposited the entire amount of the bid money and that thereafter lease deed was executed in the name of the petitioner by the Collector and that possession of the fishery was delivered to him on 27-7-1998; that, as against the acceptance of the bid of the petitioner the respondent No.6 who did not drop any tender in the 6th schedule, filed an appeal, being Revenue Miscellaneous Appeal No. 150 of 1998, before the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet alleging that the fishery has been leased out at a low amount without making proper publicity and that he is willing to take lease of the fishery at an amount of Taka 5,20,000.00, that the Divisional Commissioner passed order in the appeal so filed suspending approval of the lease and that also made direction to place the matter before him on 16-7-1998, that the Divisional Commissioner disposed of the appeal on 12-8-1998 upon making order for leasing the fishery afresh upon making, good publicity of the Tender, that as against the order of the Divisional Commissioner, petitioner went on appeal before the Land Appeal Board, that the said appeal was disposed of by the Member, Land Appeal Board on 22-3-1999 dismissing the same and thereupon affirming the order of the Divisional Commissioner. The petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of the Member Land Appeal Board has moved this Court and obtained the Rule. 

 3. Respondent No. 6 has entered appearance and has filed Affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the officials at the District level without waiting for approval by the Divisional Commissioner of the bid made by the petitioner executed lease agreement and that in spite of the order suspending approval delivered possession of the fishery to the petitioner, that he and others could hot make offer in the 6th schedule as because officials at the District level did not sell Tender Form to him and others on the ground of pendency of a case before the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet; that at the 6th schedule only two tenders were dropped and that of the said two participants in the 6th schedule petitioner's bid was for Taka 3,40,500.00, that officials at the district level prior to approval of the bid of the petitioner and that in disregard of the order that was made by the Divisional Commissioner suspending approval executed deed of lease and delivered possession of the fishery to the petitioner in violation of the instructions of the Ministry of Land relating to the leasing out of the fishery, that execution of the lease deed in favour of the petitioner prior to approval of the bid of the petitioner by the Divisional Commissioner and delivery of possession of the fishery to the petitioner in disregard of the order of the Divisional Commissioner itself shows that there was something fishy in the matter of leasing out the fishery to the petitioner; that allegation of disposing of the appeal without hearing the petitioner is not correct and that records of the fishery was transmitted to the office of the Divisional Commissioner for approval of the bids that was made by the petitioner and another in the 6th schedule and that the Divisional Commissioner on scrutiny of the papers having been satisfied that the bid recommended for approval was too low and that there having been insufficient publicity of the Tender calling bid for leasing out the fishery number of participants in the auction of the fishery was poor and did not approve, in that background of the facts and circumstances bid of the petitioner and that made order for calling fresh tender for the purpose of leasing out the fishery afresh, that the Divisional Commissioner also made order for selling tender at different places including in the office of the Divisional Commissioner, that the writ petition is not maintainable since petitioner has not availed of the forum provided in section 6 of the Appeal Board Act, 1989 (Act No. XXIV of 1989) that the petitioner could have applied for the Review of the order of the Member of the Land Appeal Board by way of preferring Review before the full Board of the Land Appeal Board consisting of the Chairman and the two Members of the Land Appeal Board, that the respondents did not accept the bid of the petitioner or, in other words, did not approve the process of auction of the fishery held in the 6th schedule, that in the 6th schedule although petitioner's bid was highest but the same was shockingly low in comparison to the bids of previous years and for that Divisional Commissioner did not approve petitioner's bid. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that in view of the Memorandum dated 24-9-1994 (Annexure-D to the petition) of the Ministry of Land as the Tender Committee was quite competent in a case where even at the 3rd schedule 25% higher amount over the amount at which in the previous year`s fishery was leased out was not offered by the participants in the auction of the fishery then upon consideration of the area and location of the fishery as well as other attending circumstances to accept the offer at the subsequent schedule i.e. offer made at the 4th schedule, and that as in the instant case even at the 6th schedule that having had no offer at 25% higher over the amount i.e. Taka 5,20,000.00 at which fishery in question was leased out in the previous term the tender, committee correctly considered the offer that was made by the petitioner at an amount of Taka 3,40,500.00 and that then having accepted the said offer and that thereupon having had executed the deed of lease and that having had delivered possession of the fishery to the petitioner the Divisional Commissioner (respondent No.3) and the respondent No. 2 Member, Land Appeal Board were not correct in refusing to approve and accept petitioner's bid and that further in making the order for leasing out the fishery afresh upon calling fresh offer through well circulated tender notice. He also submits since the petitioner on the execution of the lease deed and that upon delivery of possession bas acquired a vested right in the fishery in question the respondents were not correct in rejecting the recommendation of the Tender Committee for according approval to the bid of the petitioner. He further submits that the Divisional Commissioner having had not approved the highest bid that was made by the petition and recommended by the Tender Committee and that having had made the order for leasing out the fishery afresh upon inviting bid through well circulated tender without hearing the petitioner and that thereby having had violated the principle Of natural justice the said order of the Divisional Commissioner not being legal and that said illegal order of the Divisional Commissioner having been affirmed by the Member, Land Appeal Board the same was also not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate lastly, submits that the Member, Land Appeal Board failed to take into consideration the Memorandum dated 28-9-1994 wherein there were specific instructions to the Tender Committee at the District level to. lease out a fishery at the highest bid made in an auction in the 4th schedule and that in the case of the instant fishery the Tender Committee made recommendation for approval of the bid of the petitioner made in an auction in the 6th schedule being the highest among the bids made the Divisional Commissioner without hearing the petitioner and that only on the allegation of the respondent No. 6 that the fishery was leased out at a shockingly low price acted illegally in not according approval to the bid that was made by the petitioner in the 6th schedule. 

 6. Learned Advocate for the respondent No. 6 has submitted that admitted position being that lease deed was executed prior to the approval of the bid (hat was made by the petitioner in the 6th schedule, by the prescribed authority and that possession of the-fishery was also made over to petitioner at a time when petitioner's bid was not approved by the Divisional Commissioner and, as such, even if lease deed was executed in favour of the petitioner and that possession of the fishery was made over to the petitioner but by that petitioner did not acquire any right of any kind in the fishery and that further, the approving authority i.e. Divisional Commissioner did not approve the bid of the petitioner made in the 6th schedule in the background of the facts and circumstances that the bid amount being too low with reference to the amount at which the fishery in question was leased out in-the previous years and that the auction at the 6th schedule wherein petitioner and another were participants and made bids, having been held without wide circulation of Tender notice inviting bid/for leasing out the fishery-and, as such, the respondent No.3 Was quite within his competency in not according approval to the bid of the petitioner and that later on the respondent No. 2 was also correct in not interfering with the order of the respondent No. 3. He continues that in making the order for calling fresh bid to lease out the fishery through wide circulation of tender in the background of the admitted fact that the amount at which the fishery in question was leased out for year 1402-1404 was at Taka 5,20,000.00 and that the bid of the petitioner for the years 1405-1407 was at Taka 3,40,500.00 the respondents have not committed any illegality. 

 7. It is the contention of the petitioner that even at the 6th schedule when there was no bid at 25% higher over the amount for which the fishery was leased out for the year 1402-1404 or that at an amount higher than the previous term and that at the 6th schedule petitioner's bid was being the highest the tender committee in the light of the instruction in the memorandum dated 28-9-1994 (Annexure-D) of the Ministry of Land, wherein it was clearly mentioned that in case at the 4th schedule bid in respect of a fishery if not even though 25% higher than the lease amount of the previous terms the tender committee in consideration of the location and area of a particular fishery as well as the attending circumstances would be competent to lease out the fishery to the highest bidder at the said schedule, having had recommended for approval of his bid the Divisional Commissioner ought to have approved the bid made by him at the 6th schedule and that the Divisional Commissioner (respondent No. 3) as well as the Member; Land Appeal Board (respondent No. 2) having had acted contrary to the instruction of the Ministry of aforementioned Memo the actions of the respondents were illegal. 

 8. From the reading of the Memorandum (Annexure D to the petition) it is seen that in case at the 4th schedule bid in respect of a particular fishery is not 25% higher over the lease amount, of the previous term the Tender Committee may consider the bid so made in the 4th schedule or subsequent schedules and may lease out the fishery at the said bid amount. But there is nothing in the memo dated 28-9-94 (Annexure-D) that in a situation spelt out there in a fishery would be leased out prior to approval of the bid or that prior to acceptance of the bid by the prescribed authority or designated person, herein undisputedly, the Divisional Commissioner, (respondent No. 3). There is also nothing in the memorandum (Annexure D) that approving authority has no option to consider the sufficiency of the bid but that he is to give approval to the bid recommended by the tender committee. In the instant case, the approving authority did not accord approval to the recommendation of the Tender committee or, in other words, did not approve the bid of the petitioner on the ground that the bid of the petitioner was too low in comparison to the lease amount of previous term and the tender notice as regard auction of the fishery in question at the 6th schedule was not well circulated. The facts that weighed with the approving authority in not according approval to the recommendation of the tender committee for approving bid of the petitioner or, in other words, for acceptance of the bid of the petitioner as cannot be said arbitrary or that lacked reasonableness, in our view, the actions of the respondents cannot be said illegal or that the actions legality whereof questioned were beyond their competency. As law does not require that matter of non-approval or non-acceptance of a bid made in an auction is to be made with notice to the bidder or, in other words, bidder is to be allowed to present his case as regard the reasonableness of his bid before the approving authority in case of non-approval or non-acceptance of a bid, nor it being the requirement of law that competent authority prior to the making of an order for calling fresh tender inviting fresh bid upon disapproving the bid made by a person in an auction held earlier would give hearing to such person, nor there being any question of condemning or punishing a person unheard in a case of non-approving or non-accepting of the bid of such person made in an auction by the prescribed authority, as such, we are of the view that petitioner's contention of violation of principle of Natural Justice in the making of the order by the respondent No. 3 and as affirmed by the respondent No. 2 is not a well founded one Petitioner's contention that his vested right in the fishery has been violated is also not well-conceived one in that by the execution of lease deed in his favour and that by the delivery of possession of the fishery to him prior to the approval of the bid made by the petitioner in the auction held for leasing out the fishery or, in other words, prior to acceptance of the bid by the authority no right of any kind in the fishery was created in his favour. 

 9. The learned Advocate for the petitioner does not dispute the fact that bid that was made by the petitioner in respect of the fishery in question was required to be approved by the Divisional Commissioner. It is not also disputed that prior to approval of the bid of the petitioner by the Divisional Commissioner lease deed was executed by the Collector in respect of the fishery in favour of the petitioner and that possession of fishery was delivered to the petitioner. It is seen from the order of the Divisional Commissioner as well as from the order of the Member, Land Appeal Board that in the 6th schedule petitioner made the bid in respect of the fishery in question in response to a tender that was not widely circulated and consequent thereupon bid that was made by the petitioner was though highest but too low in comparison to previous term and for that the approving authority Divisional Commissioner, as well as the appellate authority did not approve the bid and that made order for calling fresh bid through widely circulated tender. In our opinion, in the background of the facts action that was taken by the approving authority and that affirmed by the appellate authority can hardly be said or considered contrary to normal course of action. The approving authority was quite within its jurisdiction in not approving the bid of the petitioner on the ground of the bid being of low amount. In the aforestate of the matter in our view the approving authority was quite within its jurisdiction in not approving the bid that was made by the petitioner in respect of the fishery in question. Since petitioner's bid was not ultimately approved by the prescribed approving authority, so even if lease deed was executed in favour of the petitioner in respect of the fishery in question and that possession was delivered to him before approval of bid that was made by him in the 6th schedule thereby he did not acquire any right in the fishery in question. 

 The decision referred to by the learned Advocate would have been a relevant one had there been any case of violation of principle of natural justice in the instant case in the background of the facts that emerged from the materials on record. We have already mentioned that lease deed in respect of the fishery in question was executed in favour of the petitioner and that possession of the fishery was delivered to him prior to the approval of the bid that was made by the petitioner. The undisputed fact is that petitioner's bid in respect of the fishery was not approved by the authority. Since by mere milking bid in an auction no right is created in the subject matter of the auction and that so long the bid of a person is approved or accepted no right or interest in the subject matter of the auction is created in favour of the bidder, as such, by execution of lease deed and delivery of possession of the fishery to the petitioner prior to approval or acceptance of the bid of the petitioner by the prescribed authority no right, not to speak of vested as contended by the petitioner, was created in favour of the petitioner in the fishery. It is not the requirement of law that approving authority in making its decision as to disapproving of bid would make such decision upon giving hearing to the petition. In the afore state of the matter as by the lease deed that as executed in favour of the petitioner and that possession of the fishery that was-made over to the petitioner prior to approval of the bid the petitioner did not acquire any right of any kind in the fishery in question his contention of that action of the Divisional Commissioner violated vested right of the petitioner is not a merited one.
